questions.question: Who among the following persons was elected, unopposed, as the President of Hockey India in November 2020?

• **Gyanendro Ningombamwas elected, unopposed, as the President of Hockey India in November 2020**.

 
 
• **Gyanendro Ningombam** has been elected unopposed as the new President of Hockey India, replacing the former President Mohd Mushtaque Ahmad, who now moves to the senior vice-president position on the Executive Board.
 
• Hockey India recently held its 10th Congress and elections in New Delhi, with access to the video conference meeting being made available for members who were unable to travel due to COVID-19 restrictions.
 
• Ningombam is now the** first President of Hockey India** from the northeast region of the country and previously held the position of officiating President after Ahmed tendered his resignation in July.
 
• Now elected for a two-year term, he has previously served as the chief executive of Manipur Hockey between 2009 and 2014 and has been associated with the governing body for over a decade.
 
• He follows Ahmad's reign which included overseeing the hosting of the International Hockey Federation Men's World Cup in 2018.

• He switched to Air India in 1990 and later became the company's senior manager.
 
• Singh made his international debut at the 1990 Asian Games in Beijing, where India won silver.
 
• He represented the Indian hockey team in 43 matches before retiring at the age of 26 citing "too much politics in hockey."

questions.question: As of January 2020, who held the title of India's youngest chess grandmaster?

• **Dommaraju Gukesh** (born 29 May 2006), commonly referred to as Gukesh D, is a chess player from India.
 
• He is the **second** youngest person in history to be given the title of Grandmaster by** FIDE** in March 2019.
 
• At **12 years, 7 months and 17 days**, D. Gukesh became India's youngest Grandmaster on **15 January 2019**.
 
• With this accomplishment, Gukesh has overtaken **Praggnanandhaa**, who holds the record in June 2018 at 12 years and 10 months. 
 
• In the Under 12 category, Gukesh won the Under-9 division of the **Asian School Chess Championship** in 2015 and the **World Youth Chess Championship** in 2018.
 
• At the **2018 Asian Youth Chess Championships**, he also won five gold medals, in the U-12 individual rapid and blitz, U-12 team rapid and blitz, and the U-12 classical individual formats.
 
• In March 2018, at the **34th Cappelle-la-Grande Open**, he completed the criteria for the title of International Master.
 
• As the youngest grandmaster ever, Gukesh nearly surpassed **Sergey Karjakin** but missed the record by 17 days.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian woman wrestler to win a medal at the Olympics?
questions.solution: The Correct answer is **Sakshi Malik.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Sakshi Malik **was the first Indian Women Wrestler to win Medal in Olympics. • She won this medal **in 2016 Olympics held in Rio de Janeiro**. • She won the Bronze medal in **56 kg weight freestyle wrestling category.** • She had honoured with Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award **(**presently known as **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award) **and **Padma Shri in 2017.**
